26-qf2-qb-1612.solution: Total sales = A + B + C + D = 200 + 300 + 250 + 400. Adding in pairs, 200 + 400 = 600 and 300 + 250 = 550. So the total is 600 + 550 = ₦1,150.
26-qf2-qb-1612.trick: Eliminate first: the total cannot be less than the biggest bar (400), so ₦250 is out, and it cannot be more than 4 × 400 = 1,600, so ₦4,120 is out. That leaves ₦1,150.

26-qf2-qb-1622.solution: Critical points are where f′(x) = 0. Here f′(x) = 3x² − 18x + 24 = 3(x² − 6x + 8) = 3(x − 2)(x − 4). So f′(x) = 0 at x = 2 and x = 4.
26-qf2-qb-1622.trick: Divide f′ by 3 to get x² − 6x + 8. The two roots must add up to 6, and only 2 and 4 do that. The pair 2 and 6 adds to 8, and 4 and 8 adds to 12.

26-qf2-qb-1630.solution: Maximum height H = (u sin θ)² ÷ (2g), using g = 9.8 m/s². The upward speed is 20 × sin 30° = 20 × 0.5 = 10 m/s. So H = 10² ÷ (2 × 9.8) = 100 ÷ 19.6 ≈ 5.1 m.
26-qf2-qb-1630.trick: The upward speed is half of 20, so 10 m/s. Then H = 100 ÷ 19.6, which is just over 5 because 19.6 is just under 20. Only 5.1 m fits.

26-qf2-qb-1639.solution: For a binomial distribution the standard deviation is √(npq), where q = 1 − p. Here n = 1,600 and p = q = 0.5, so npq = 1,600 × 0.25 = 400. So the standard deviation is √400 = 20.
26-qf2-qb-1639.trick: When p = 0.5, the standard deviation is just √n ÷ 2. √1,600 = 40, and half of 40 is 20.

26-qf2-qb-1650.solution: One km/h is 1,000 m in 3,600 s, which is 1 ÷ 3.6 m/s. So divide by 3.6: 360 ÷ 3.6 = 100 m/s.
26-qf2-qb-1650.trick: Divide by 3.6. Since 3.6 × 100 = 360, the answer is 100.

26-qf2-qb-1664.solution: For a binomial distribution, variance = npq, where q = 1 − p = 0.3. So variance = 80 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 80 × 0.21 = 16.8.

26-qf2-qb-1703.solution: Take the 800 MW as the electrical output, which is 40% of the heat put in. So heat input = 800 ÷ 0.4 = 2,000 MW. Waste = 2,000 − 800 = 1,200 MW. Over one hour that is 1,200 MWh.
26-qf2-qb-1703.trick: The 800 MW is the useful 40%, so the wasted 60% is 1.5 times as big: 800 × 1.5 = 1,200 MW, which is 1,200 MWh in an hour. The total heat input is only 2,000 MWh, so 2,400 and 3,600 are too big.

26-qf2-qb-1707.solution: Coefficient of variation CV = (standard deviation ÷ mean) × 100%. So standard deviation = 30% × mean = 0.30 × 60 = 18.

26-qf2-qb-1714.solution: Time = distance ÷ speed = 50 ÷ 80 = 0.625 hours. One hour is 3,600 seconds, so 0.625 × 3,600 = 2,250 seconds.
26-qf2-qb-1714.trick: At 80 km/h each kilometre takes 3,600 ÷ 80 = 45 seconds. So 50 km takes 50 × 45 = 2,250 seconds.

26-qf2-qb-1747.solution: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B). So P(rain on both days) = 0.4 × 0.3 = 0.12.
26-qf2-qb-1747.trick: 4 × 3 = 12, and each number has one decimal place, so the answer has two: 0.12.

26-qf2-qb-1751.solution: Standard deviation measures how far the values spread from the mean. If every value is 7, the mean is 7 and every deviation is 0. So the variance is 0 and the standard deviation is 0.
26-qf2-qb-1751.trick: Identical values have no spread, and no spread means a standard deviation of 0. That rules out 49 and 256 straight away.

26-qf2-qb-1754.trick: Test the options. ⁴C₄ = 1 and ⁶C₄ = 15 are both far below 70, so the answer is 8. Check: 8 × 7 × 6 × 5 ÷ 24 = 70.

26-qf2-qb-1770.trick: Subtract part by part. All three options start with 4, so only the second part matters: −2 − 1 = −3.

26-qf2-qb-1790.solution: The 30 who study Math include the 10 who also study Physics. So only Math = 30 − 10 = 20 students.
26-qf2-qb-1790.trick: Take the overlap off the Math total: 30 − 10 = 20. The Physics number is not needed.

26-qf2-qb-1795.solution: Inverse variation means P × V is constant. So k = 8 × 4 = 32. At V = 10: P = 32 ÷ 10 = 3.2 atm.
26-qf2-qb-1795.trick: The volume goes from 4 to 10, which is 2.5 times bigger, so divide the pressure by 2.5: 8 ÷ 2.5 = 3.2. Pressure must fall when volume rises, so 20 atm is out.

26-qf2-qb-1801.solution: The ratio 2 : 3 has 2 + 3 = 5 parts. One part is 5 kg ÷ 5 = 1 kg. Cashews are 2 parts, so 2 × 1 = 2 kg.
26-qf2-qb-1801.trick: 5 parts in a 5 kg mix means 1 kg a part, so the 2 cashew parts are 2 kg.

26-qf2-qb-1809.solution: Work = ∫ F dx from x = 1 to x = 3 = ∫ 4x dx = [2x²] from 1 to 3. That is 2(3²) − 2(1²) = 18 − 2 = 16 J.
26-qf2-qb-1809.trick: F = 4x is a straight line, so work = average force × distance. The average force is F at the middle, x = 2, which is 8 N, and the distance is 2 m. So 8 × 2 = 16 J.

26-qf2-qb-1830.solution: Power = work done ÷ time = mgh ÷ t. So P = 1,000 × 9.8 × 5 ÷ 10 = 49,000 ÷ 10 = 4,900 W.
26-qf2-qb-1830.trick: The weight is 1,000 × 9.8 = 9,800 N. The height gained is 5 m in 10 s, which is 0.5 m/s, so the power is 9,800 × 0.5 = 4,900 W.

26-qf2-qb-1841.solution: Area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂, where d₁ and d₂ are the diagonals. So area = ½ × 10 × 24 = 120 cm².

26-qf2-bm-2077.solution: f′(x) = 3x² − 12x + 9 = 3(x − 1)(x − 3), so the critical points are x = 1 and x = 3. The second derivative is f″(x) = 6x − 12. At x = 3 it is 6, which is positive, so that is a minimum. At x = 1 it is −6, which is negative, so the local maximum is at x = 1.
26-qf2-bm-2077.trick: f′ = 3(x − 1)(x − 3), so the critical points are 1 and 3. This cubic has a positive x³ term, so it rises, falls, then rises again, which makes the smaller critical point the maximum: x = 1. Also 0 is out, because f′(0) = 9 is not zero.

26-qf2-bm-2083.trick: 450 is 3 times 150, so the increase is 2 times the original, which is 200%. A figure of 300% would be the new size as a percentage of the old, not the increase.

26-qf2-bm-2089.solution: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: a = dv/dt = 6t − 12. At t = 2: a = 6(2) − 12 = 0 m/s².
26-qf2-bm-2089.trick: Differentiate to get 6t − 12. At t = 2 that is 12 − 12 = 0. Or spot that v = 3t(t − 4) is zero at t = 0 and t = 4, so it turns at the midpoint t = 2, where the acceleration is 0.

26-qf2-bm-2095.trick: All three options end in 480, so only the thousands matter: 2 × 16 = 32, which gives 32,480.

26-qf2-bm-2102.solution: Wins : draws = 7 : 3. 21 wins is 21 ÷ 7 = 3 times the ratio, so draws = 3 × 3 = 9.
26-qf2-bm-2102.trick: 21 is 3 times 7, so the draws are 3 times 3, which is 9.

26-qf2-bm-2108.solution: The culture grew by a factor of (1.6 × 10⁶) ÷ (2 × 10⁵) = 8. Since 8 = 2³, that is 3 doublings in 3 hours. So the doubling time is 3 ÷ 3 = 1 hour.
26-qf2-bm-2108.trick: Write 1.6 × 10⁶ as 16 × 10⁵. Then 2 to 16 is 2, 4, 8, 16, which is three doublings in 3 hours, so one hour each.
